questions.name: Real Property
questions.text: The metes and bounds method of legal description defines a parcel of land by:

answers.text: township and range grid coordinates from the government survey
a lot and block number referencing a recorded subdivision plat
courses and distances starting and ending at a designated point of beginning
street address and the county assessor's parcel identification number

explanations.a: Township and range coordinates are the rectangular survey system, not metes and bounds.
explanations.b: Lot and block is a separate description method using a recorded plat.
explanations.c: Metes and bounds traces the property boundary using compass bearings (courses) and measured distances, starting and ending at the same point of beginning.
explanations.d: Street addresses and parcel numbers are used for tax and assessment purposes but are not formal legal descriptions.

questions.name: Real Property
questions.text: In the rectangular (government) survey system, one section of land contains:

answers.text: 1 acre
640 acres
36 acres
160 acres

explanations.a: One acre is 43,560 square feet; a section is far larger.
explanations.b: A section is one square mile (5,280 × 5,280 feet = 27,878,400 square feet ÷ 43,560 = 640 acres).
explanations.c: 36 is the number of sections in a township, not the acreage of one section.
explanations.d: 160 acres is one quarter-section (a section divided into four equal quarters).

questions.name: Real Property
questions.text: A lot and block legal description identifies a parcel by:

answers.text: referring to a specific lot and block number within a recorded subdivision plat
measuring courses and distances from a surveyed point of beginning
citing the township, range, and section number from the government survey
using the county tax assessor's parcel identification number

explanations.a: Lot and block (also called plat-and-lot) descriptions refer to a lot number and block number within a subdivision plat that has been surveyed and recorded in the public records.
explanations.b: Courses and distances from a point of beginning describe the metes and bounds method.
explanations.c: Township, range, and section are the components of the rectangular survey system.
explanations.d: An assessor's parcel number is an administrative identifier for tax purposes, not a legal description method.

questions.name: Real Property
questions.text: A single-story house measures 45 feet wide by 30 feet deep. What is the gross living area (GLA)?

answers.text: 900 square feet
150 square feet
75 square feet
1,350 square feet

explanations.a: 900 square feet would result from 30 × 30 or a similar pair; 45 × 30 yields a different product.
explanations.b: 150 is the sum of the two dimensions (perimeter math), not the area.
explanations.c: 75 is half the sum, not the product of the dimensions.
explanations.d: GLA = length × width = 45 × 30 = 1,350 square feet.

questions.name: Real Property
questions.text: When measuring gross living area (GLA) for a residential appraisal, an appraiser would typically EXCLUDE:

answers.text: finished bedrooms on the second floor above grade
a finished basement, because it is located below grade
an enclosed, heated sunroom addition above grade
a den or home office on the main above-grade floor

explanations.a: Above-grade finished rooms are included in GLA regardless of their floor level.
explanations.b: FNMA guidelines and standard appraisal practice exclude below-grade finished space from GLA; a finished basement is measured and described separately.
explanations.c: A properly permitted above-grade enclosed addition is included in GLA.
explanations.d: Any above-grade finished living space, including a den or office, is counted in GLA.

questions.name: Real Property
questions.text: A rectangular parcel measures 660 feet by 660 feet. How many acres does it contain? (1 acre = 43,560 sq ft)

answers.text: 2 acres
5 acres
10 acres
43,560 acres

explanations.a: 2 acres = 87,120 square feet; 660 × 660 = 435,600 square feet, which is five times larger.
explanations.b: 5 acres = 217,800 square feet; 660 × 660 = 435,600 square feet, which is larger.
explanations.d: 43,560 acres is the number of square feet in one acre, not the acreage of this parcel.

questions.name: Real Property
questions.text: Market value in real estate is BEST defined as:

answers.text: the most probable price a property would bring in an arm's-length sale between a willing buyer and willing seller, both fully informed and acting without compulsion
the price the seller needs to net after paying off all liens and closing costs
the assessed value assigned by the local government for ad valorem tax purposes
the insurance replacement cost of the improvements on the property

explanations.a: Market value is the most probable price the property would sell for in a competitive, open market under conditions of a fair sale between informed parties who are not under duress.
explanations.b: The seller's net proceeds are based on their personal financial needs, not on market conditions or buyer demand.
explanations.c: Assessed value is set by government for taxation and may differ significantly from market value.
explanations.d: Insurance replacement cost covers the cost to rebuild improvements and is not the same as market value, which includes the land.

questions.name: Real Property
questions.text: The real estate principle that location is the most critical determinant of a property's value is expressed by the term:

answers.text: regression
substitution
anticipation
situs

explanations.a: Regression holds that a superior property surrounded by inferior ones will be pulled down in value.
explanations.b: Substitution holds that a buyer will pay no more than the cost of an equally desirable substitute property.
explanations.c: Anticipation holds that value is created by the expectation of future benefits.
explanations.d: Situs refers to the economic and social importance of location in determining real estate value — the basis for the classic phrase 'location, location, location.'

questions.name: Real Property
questions.text: A comparative market analysis (CMA) differs from a licensed appraisal in that a CMA:

answers.text: is prepared by a licensed appraiser and satisfies USPAP requirements
is prepared by a real estate licensee to help set a listing or offer price and is not a formal valuation for lending purposes
is required by mortgage lenders as the primary valuation tool before approving a loan
must be prepared in conformance with Uniform Standards of Professional Appraisal Practice

explanations.a: A CMA is prepared by a real estate agent, not a licensed appraiser; USPAP applies to appraisers.
explanations.b: A CMA is an informal market comparison used by agents to assist clients in pricing; it is not a state-regulated appraisal and is not accepted by lenders for loan underwriting.
explanations.c: Mortgage lenders require a licensed appraisal, not a CMA.
explanations.d: USPAP governs appraisers; a CMA by a salesperson is not subject to those standards.

questions.name: Real Property
questions.text: A broker price opinion (BPO) is typically used by:

answers.text: county assessors to establish assessed values for property tax purposes
homebuyers as a legally required inspection report before closing
lenders and servicers as a lower-cost tool to estimate value for asset management purposes
homeowners as the required basis for appealing an eminent domain award

explanations.a: Assessed values for tax purposes are set by government assessors, not BPOs.
explanations.b: A BPO is a valuation tool, not a home inspection report.
explanations.c: Banks and mortgage servicers use BPOs — performed by real estate brokers reviewing comparables — for decisions on defaulted loans, REO properties, and portfolio management, because they cost less than full appraisals.
explanations.d: Eminent domain proceedings require formal appraisals; a BPO is not the standard for those purposes.

questions.name: Real Property
questions.text: Personal property that has been permanently attached to real property and has legally become part of the real estate is called a:

answers.text: fixture
chattel
trade fixture
license

explanations.a: A fixture is personal property that has been affixed to real property in a permanent manner so that it becomes part of the realty and transfers with it.
explanations.b: Chattel is another word for personal property that has not been affixed to real estate.
explanations.c: A trade fixture is business equipment installed by a tenant that the tenant typically retains the right to remove.
explanations.d: A license in real estate is a personal, revocable permission to use another's land; it is not a classification of property.

questions.name: Real Property
questions.text: A tenant installs commercial refrigeration equipment in a leased restaurant space for use in the business and fails to remove it when the lease expires. The tenant's BEST argument against the landlord's claim that the equipment has become a fixture is that it is a:

answers.text: fixture permanently incorporated into the real estate
permanent improvement transferred to the landlord at lease end
chattel that remained personal property throughout the tenancy
trade fixture that the tenant had the right to remove during the tenancy

explanations.a: That is the landlord's argument, not the tenant's best defense.
explanations.b: Arguing it is a permanent improvement supports the landlord's position, not the tenant's.
explanations.c: If the equipment was attached to the building, calling it unattached chattel is harder to sustain than the trade-fixture argument.
explanations.d: Business equipment installed by a tenant to carry on a trade or business is a trade fixture, which the tenant retains the right to remove during the lease term or within a reasonable time after expiration.

questions.name: Real Property
questions.text: The sales comparison approach to appraising value is grounded in the principle of:

answers.text: anticipation, because buyers weigh expected future benefits
substitution, because a buyer will pay no more than the cost of an equally desirable alternative
contribution, because the value added by a feature equals its effect on total sale price
conformity, because properties reach maximum value when they blend with surrounding uses

explanations.a: Anticipation drives the income approach, not the sales comparison approach.
explanations.b: The sales comparison approach rests on substitution: a knowledgeable buyer will pay no more for the subject property than the cost of acquiring a comparable substitute in the market.
explanations.c: Contribution underlies the analysis of specific features in an appraisal but is not the foundational principle of the entire sales comparison method.
explanations.d: Conformity relates to how blending with surrounding land uses affects value; it is not the foundation of the sales comparison method.

questions.name: Real Property
questions.text: A comparable sale has a swimming pool, but the subject property does not. To adjust the comparable to estimate the subject's value, the appraiser should:

answers.text: add the pool's contributory value to the subject's estimated value
add the pool's contributory value to the comparable's sale price
subtract the pool's contributory value from the comparable's sale price
make no adjustment because pools are not considered in residential appraisals

explanations.a: Adjustments are made to the comparable, not directly added to the subject.
explanations.b: Adding the pool value to the comparable would make the comparable even more superior; adjustments must close the gap toward the subject.
explanations.c: The comparable is superior because it has a pool and the subject does not. To make them equivalent, the appraiser subtracts the pool's contributory value from the comparable's price.
explanations.d: Pools are a recognized amenity that affects market value and must be accounted for in adjustments.

questions.name: Real Property
questions.text: In the cost approach to appraisal, the estimated property value equals:

answers.text: land value plus the replacement or reproduction cost of improvements, minus accrued depreciation
gross income multiplied by the market capitalization rate
the average of the three adjusted comparable sales prices
replacement cost of improvements minus the outstanding mortgage balance

explanations.a: The cost approach adds the site value (land is never depreciated) to the cost new of improvements, then deducts all forms of accrued depreciation (physical, functional, and external).
explanations.b: Multiplying income by a cap rate is the income capitalization approach, not the cost approach.
explanations.c: Averaging adjusted comparables is the reconciliation step in the sales comparison approach.
explanations.d: Mortgage balance is a financing matter and has no place in the cost approach formula.

questions.name: Real Property
questions.keyword: capitalization rate NOI divided by value
questions.text: An apartment building produces $50,000 in annual net operating income and has an estimated market value of $500,000. The overall capitalization rate is:

explanations.a: 5.0% would require a $1,000,000 value at $50,000 income; here the value is $500,000.
explanations.b: 50.0% is the result if the figures are flipped; cap rate = NOI ÷ value, not value ÷ NOI.
explanations.c: 0.1% would result from dividing $500 by $500,000, not the given figures.

questions.name: Real Property
questions.text: When a lender requires an independent estimate of a property's value before approving a mortgage, the valuation must generally be performed by a:

answers.text: real estate salesperson using a comparative market analysis
licensed or certified appraiser providing a formal appraisal report
real estate broker providing a broker price opinion
title company using automated valuation model data

explanations.a: A CMA by a salesperson is not accepted by lenders as a formal valuation for loan purposes.
explanations.b: Federal law (FIRREA) requires that appraisals for federally related transactions be performed by state-licensed or state-certified appraisers.
explanations.c: A BPO may be used for certain asset-management purposes but does not substitute for a formal appraisal in most mortgage transactions.
explanations.d: Automated valuation models may be used for some low-risk transactions but are not a substitute for a licensed appraiser's formal report in standard mortgage lending.

questions.name: Real Property
questions.text: A defect in the chain of title that raises reasonable doubt about a seller's ability to convey clear ownership is called:

answers.text: an encroachment
an easement in gross
a cloud on the title
a lis pendens notice

explanations.a: An encroachment is a physical intrusion across a boundary line; it may affect title but is not itself the term for a title defect.
explanations.b: An easement in gross is a right held by an individual rather than appurtenant to land; it may be an encumbrance but is not the general term for a title defect.
explanations.c: A cloud on the title refers to any outstanding claim, lien, or defect in the chain of title that impairs the owner's ability to convey marketable title.
explanations.d: A lis pendens is a recorded notice of pending litigation; it is one specific type of cloud, not the general term.

questions.name: Real Property
questions.text: A buyer discovers a lis pendens recorded against a property she is under contract to purchase. This notice indicates:

answers.text: a pending lawsuit that may affect ownership or title to the property
a zoning change that will restrict the property's permitted uses
a mechanics lien filed by an unpaid contractor
a utility easement recorded in favor of the electric company

explanations.a: Lis pendens means 'suit pending.' It is recorded to warn prospective buyers and lenders that litigation affecting title is in progress, and that any interest acquired during the pendency takes subject to the outcome.
explanations.b: Zoning changes are recorded through the local government's zoning records, not a lis pendens.
explanations.c: A mechanic's lien is recorded separately and in a different form from a lis pendens.
explanations.d: Utility easements are recorded as separate instruments in the deed records.

questions.name: Real Property
questions.text: When a deed is recorded in the public land records, it provides:

answers.text: the buyer with automatic title insurance at no additional cost
proof that the deed was witnessed by a state-licensed notary
a guarantee that no prior unrecorded interests exist against the property
constructive notice to the world of the grantee's ownership claim

explanations.a: Recording does not confer title insurance; that requires a separate policy purchase.
explanations.b: Acknowledgment before a notary is a prerequisite for recording in most states, but recording itself does not prove execution was proper.
explanations.c: Recording protects against subsequent claimants but does not guarantee that prior unrecorded interests do not exist.
explanations.d: Recording imparts constructive notice — a legal presumption that everyone in the world is aware of the recorded document — protecting the grantee against later purchasers and lienholders.

questions.name: Real Property
questions.text: A lender's title insurance policy differs from an owner's title insurance policy in that the lender's policy:

answers.text: protects the buyer against all title defects that arise after closing
insures the lender's security interest and decreases in coverage as the loan balance is paid down
provides the same coverage to the buyer that an owner's policy would
is issued at no additional cost when the owner's policy is purchased

explanations.a: Title insurance generally covers defects that existed before the policy date; it does not cover defects arising after closing.
explanations.b: A lender's policy protects the mortgagee's interest in the amount of the outstanding loan balance, which declines as payments are made; it does not protect the owner's equity.
explanations.c: The lender's policy benefits only the lender; the buyer's personal equity is not covered without a separate owner's policy.
explanations.d: A lender's policy and an owner's policy are separate products; purchasing one does not include the other automatically.

questions.name: Real Property
questions.text: A general warranty deed offers the broadest protection to the grantee because the grantor:

answers.text: warrants title only against claims arising during the grantor's period of ownership
makes no warranties whatsoever and conveys only whatever interest the grantor may hold
covenants to defend the grantee's title against all claims, including those arising before the grantor acquired the property
warrants that the property is free of all zoning and land use restrictions

explanations.a: Warranting only against claims during the grantor's ownership describes a special (limited) warranty deed.
explanations.b: Making no warranties and conveying only the grantor's existing interest describes a quitclaim deed.
explanations.c: A general warranty deed contains the fullest covenants: the grantor promises to defend title against all adverse claims from any source, whether arising before or during the grantor's ownership.
explanations.d: Zoning and land use restrictions are public law matters; no deed warranty covers freedom from all governmental regulations.

questions.name: Real Property
questions.text: A quitclaim deed conveys:

answers.text: only whatever interest the grantor holds at the time of delivery, with no warranties of title whatsoever
fee simple title with the same covenants as a general warranty deed
full ownership free of all encumbrances as of the date of recording
ownership of the improvements only, excluding the underlying land

explanations.a: A quitclaim deed releases and conveys only the grantor's existing interest, whatever that may be, without any representation or warranty about the quality of title.
explanations.b: A quitclaim deed carries no warranties; it is the opposite of a general warranty deed in terms of seller protection offered.
explanations.c: A quitclaim deed makes no statement about encumbrances; the grantee takes the interest subject to all existing claims.
explanations.d: A quitclaim deed conveys whatever the grantor owns in the property, which normally includes the land; it does not distinguish between land and improvements.

questions.name: Real Property
questions.text: Real property transferred to a beneficiary under the terms of a valid will is said to be:

answers.text: assigned
distributed by intestate succession
conveyed by adverse possession
devised to the beneficiary

explanations.a: Assignment transfers contractual rights, not testamentary ownership of real property.
explanations.b: Intestate succession applies when a person dies without a valid will; distribution under a will uses different terminology.
explanations.c: Adverse possession is a method of acquiring title through long, open, hostile use — not through inheritance.
explanations.d: The act of giving real property by will is called a devise; the recipient is the devisee.

questions.name: Real Property
questions.text: A buyer who purchases real property at a court-ordered foreclosure sale typically receives title through a:

answers.text: general warranty deed from the former owner
sheriff's deed or trustee's deed conveying the court's interest without warranty
special warranty deed issued by the lending institution
quitclaim deed executed by the defaulting borrower

explanations.a: A general warranty deed from the former owner is unlikely; the former owner has lost the property through foreclosure.
explanations.b: In a judicial foreclosure, the court issues a sheriff's deed; in a non-judicial foreclosure, the trustee issues a trustee's deed. Neither carries title warranties.
explanations.c: The lender does not typically issue a special warranty deed at the foreclosure sale itself; that might occur if the lender later sells REO property.
explanations.d: The defaulting borrower would typically not voluntarily execute a quitclaim; the sale is court-ordered, not voluntary.

questions.name: Real Property
questions.text: To acquire title by adverse possession, the claimant's use of the property must generally be:

answers.text: permissive, continuous, and supported by a written license from the owner
occasional, notorious, and made under a recorded deed of trust
open, notorious, hostile, exclusive, and continuous for the statutory period
partial, shared with the owner, and for at least 100 years

explanations.a: Permissive use negates the hostile element required for adverse possession; it cannot ripen into title.
explanations.b: Adverse possession requires continuous use, not merely occasional use; it also does not require a recorded instrument.
explanations.c: The elements of adverse possession are typically remembered as ONCHA: Open, Notorious, Continuous, Hostile (against the owner's interest), and for the statutory period (varies by state, often 7–21 years).
explanations.d: Shared use with the owner and 100-year periods are not the standard requirements; hostility and exclusivity are required.

questions.name: Real Property
questions.text: At closing, the current year's property taxes have not yet been paid. The seller's prorated share of taxes for the portion of the year they owned the property typically appears on the closing statement as:

answers.text: a credit to the buyer and a debit to the seller
a debit to both the buyer and the seller in equal amounts
a credit to the seller and a debit to the buyer
an off-statement adjustment handled directly between the parties

explanations.a: Because taxes are paid in arrears and the seller owes for the period they owned the property, the seller is debited (charged) for that portion, and the buyer receives a credit (since the buyer will pay the full annual bill when it comes due).
explanations.b: Only the seller is debited for the pre-closing period; the buyer receives a credit, not a charge.
explanations.c: A credit to the seller and a debit to the buyer would have the buyer compensating the seller, which is the reverse of the correct proration direction.
explanations.d: Prorations are standard closing statement entries, not off-statement adjustments.

questions.name: Real Property
questions.text: The principle of substitution holds that when several similar properties are available at different prices, an informed buyer will:

answers.text: pay a premium for the most architecturally unique property in the market
select the highest-priced property as an indicator of superior quality
favor newly constructed properties over existing homes regardless of price
pay no more for a property than the price of an equally desirable substitute

explanations.a: Uniqueness may actually limit marketability; substitution holds that comparable alternatives set a ceiling on what a buyer will pay.
explanations.b: A rational buyer does not pay more simply because a price is high; substitution assumes informed buyers select value.
explanations.c: New construction preference is not part of the principle of substitution; it applies equally to all comparable properties regardless of age.
explanations.d: Substitution is the foundation of the sales comparison approach: competition among similar properties sets a ceiling on value because buyers will choose the less expensive option among equals.
